clues.name: The Kitten
clues.context: Whiskers that smell like fresh milk.
clues.inspectorDescription: A very small cat with very milky whiskers. She was somewhere milky tonight, and recently.

clues.name: The Old Dog
clues.context: Asleep on the only rug in the void.
clues.inspectorDescription: He has been asleep since before the academy was built. His paws are dry and enormous.

clues.name: The Tipped Saucer
clues.context: Flat on its back in a thin white lake.
clues.inspectorDescription: A saucer, capsized. The milk went everywhere. The saucer is not talking.

clues.name: The Water Bowl
clues.inspectorDescription: Nothing happened to the water bowl. Not everything you write down is the answer.

clues.name: The Zoomies - 3:00 AM
clues.context: Tiny wet prints in three tight circles, then gone.
clues.inspectorDescription: Paw prints leave the milk in a spiral and accelerate toward nothing in particular. That is not walking.

clues.name: Hunger
clues.context: A stomach growling like distant thunder.
clues.inspectorDescription: The old dog is hungry the way mountains are tall - permanently, and without doing anything about it.

clues.name: The Training Floor
clues.context: A white floor with exactly one thing wrong with it.
clues.inspectorDescription: The Hall of Basics. Nothing here is real except the lesson.

clues.name: The Wind
clues.context: It has been through here, and recently.
clues.inspectorDescription: The curtain is still moving. The wind takes credit for a great many things it did do, and a few it did not.

clues.name: The Mailman
clues.inspectorDescription: A cutout propped against nothing. Somebody wanted him to look guilty, which is different from being guilty.

clues.name: The Open Window
clues.context: Open, in a room with no weather.
clues.inspectorDescription: The window stands open. The curtain does its ghost impression. Something came through, or left.

clues.name: The Loose Latch
clues.context: It would not stop a determined moth.
clues.inspectorDescription: The latch hangs by one screw. It has given up, professionally speaking.

clues.name: Blaming the Wind
clues.context: A note on the sill: 'the wind did it, probably.'
clues.inspectorDescription: Somebody pinned a note blaming the wind. Blaming the wind is an old trick. The oldest.

finalSolveSentence: The graduate concludes: [The Kitten] tipped over [The Saucer] because of [The Zoomies].
